questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook tasty meals with insects at home
Where different vegetables come from and how they're grown
What we might eat in future and how food trends are predicted
Why people in Britain are eating less red meat these days
questions.why: They discuss the future of food with a food futurologist.

questions.q: How does Sam first answer Neil's question about the future of food?
options: She talks about growing meat in labs
She jokes that she'll have a sandwich soon
She says she's never thought about it
She describes insect-based foods
questions.why: She says she might have a sandwich 'in about 30 minutes in the future'.

questions.q: Why might we need to change our diets, according to Neil?
options: Food is getting more expensive every single year
People are getting less healthy and more overweight
Farmers are growing less food because of low prices
The population is growing and the climate is changing
questions.why: He mentions the increasing world population and the negative effects of climate change.

questions.q: What two things does Dr Morgaine Gaye think about?
options: What we will eat in the future and why
How to cook food and how to sell it
Food prices and food safety
Which foods are healthy and which are not
questions.why: She says she thinks about not just what we'll be eating but why.

questions.q: Who is especially interested in Dr Gaye's predictions?
options: Restaurant owners
Large companies
Governments
Farmers
questions.why: She says 'when I work for large companies, that's what they want to know.'

questions.q: How does Dr Gaye start predicting a trend?
options: With a hunch she then tries to prove or disprove
By doing large surveys of shoppers in supermarkets
By copying food trends from other countries
By asking top chefs what they plan to cook next
questions.why: She says there's an element of a hunch, then proving or disproving it.

questions.q: Why is the food business more restricted, according to Dr Gaye?
options: Food is very expensive to transport around the world
Companies don't trust each other to share their ideas
It's about safety, because we put food into our bodies
There is far too much competition between supermarkets
questions.why: She says it's about safety because 'we're ingesting that'.

questions.q: What effect do strict laws in the UK have?
options: New foods become cheaper for shoppers to buy
Companies stop creating new products altogether
Foods from abroad are banned from supermarkets
It takes longer to get a new food onto the shelves
questions.why: She says it takes longer to get from an idea to a product on the shelves.
